figurative_meaning_en: The most cherished or beloved person
example_sentences_in_english: My daughter is the apple of my eye.
He is the apple of his family's eye.
history: Originating from Vaishnava devotion in Bengali culture, where Lord Krishna represents the ultimate beloved, symbolizing profound emotional attachment.
note: The idiom draws from the dark complexion of Krishna, metaphorically extending to someone as vital and adored as life itself.
